traits.bark_colour.note: The bark colour chosen by eye for appearance (see its note), as a screen colour: it stood as appearance.bark [0.35, 0.3, 0.27], which is linear light, so the trunk drew pale grey to white beside photographs of the species (2026-10-23). It stands here in sRGB, as bark colours are picked, and the bark rule (tracheophyta) turns it into linear light.

traits.leaf_habit.note: Wikipedia, Nothofagus pumilio (read 2026-10-18): "a deciduous tree or shrub", native from 35 to 56 degrees South.

traits.leaf_colour_autumn.note: Wikipedia, Nothofagus pumilio (read 2026-10-18): the leaves "turn to yellow and reddish tones in autumn". Colour ours.

traits.leaf_out_months.note: Wikipedia, Nothofagus pumilio (read 2026-10-18): a deciduous tree of the southern Andes, so it leafs out in the southern spring; October and November, with its flowers (flowering_months 10 to 12), are ours.

traits.leaf_fall_months.note: Wikipedia, Nothofagus pumilio (read 2026-10-18): it turns and sheds its leaves in the southern autumn; April and May are ours.

traits.wood_density_basic_kg_m3.note: GWDD v.2.2 species aggregate for Nothofagus pumilio (gwddagg_v2.2_species.csv, read): specific gravity 0.49 (wsg_est, the database's hierarchical-model species mean, from 11 records in 7 sources); trunks 0.49, branches 0.51. Basic density (oven-dry mass over green volume) is the specific gravity times 1000 kg/m3.

generator.params.path_half.note: A choice of the model's (crown form step B, broadleaf revision 11): the wood from the base at which a shoot's nodes are half as long, fitted so the plant grows to the height of its oldest reference size, with the crown's width left to grow inside the loose region.

generator.params.note: Hand-set from general knowledge of the species: a deciduous southern beech of the Patagonian Andes, a tall forest tree where sheltered but, at the tree line and on the windward plains, a low, leaning tree flagged by the westerlies, its crown streaming downwind; small crinkled leaves turning red in autumn. Grown here in a steady wind. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: Rough heights from general knowledge of the species: about 5 m at 20 years and 8 m at 60, wind-pruned. Wide tolerances.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye from photographs: fresh green leaves, grey bark. Bark pattern (plant roadmap P4, `bark_pattern`): dark grey bark with lenticels, smooth when young and fissured on old trees; set from general knowledge of the species, not measured. Leaf families (plant roadmap P4, `families`): sun leaves smaller and narrower than shade leaves; set from general knowledge of sun and shade leaves and juvenile foliage, not measured.

taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.note: Barthélémy and colleagues' study of the Patagonian species: past the first leaves above the cotyledons, the leaves alternate in two ranks along the stem; unlike its relatives, this species seldom sets them in three.
